title: How a Spark application runs
goal: Explain who does what in a Spark application, trace one action from your code to running tasks, and say how Spark survives a lost executor.

items.title: Spark architecture, SparkSession, driver vs executor (20 min)
items.text: Learn: The driver plans and schedules, executors run the tasks, and the SparkSession is your entry point.
asks: Explain the Driver vs. Executor relationship.

items.title: Transformations, actions, lazy evaluation, narrow vs wide (25 min)
items.text: Learn: Nothing runs until an action is called, and wide operations need a shuffle.
asks: What is the difference between a Transformation and an Action?

items.title: Job lifecycle and fault tolerance (30 min)
items.text: Learn: An action becomes stages and tasks, and lineage lets Spark recompute only the lost partitions.

links.label: The original Spark paper (read sections 2.1, 4 and 5.1)

asks: Explain the lifecycle of a Spark Job.
How does Spark handle fault tolerance?

items.title: Where tasks run: data locality (10 min)
items.text: Learn: Spark prefers to run a task where its data already is, and waits a few seconds before settling for a worse place.

title: How Spark plans a query: Catalyst and Tungsten
goal: Name every decision between your code and the running tasks: which rewrites Catalyst makes, how physical operators are chosen, and how Tungsten executes them.
theme: How Spark plans a query: Catalyst and Tungsten

items.title: The Catalyst optimizer (25 min)
items.text: Learn: Four phases: analysis, logical optimization, physical planning and code generation.

links.label: Deep Dive into Spark SQL's Catalyst Optimizer

asks: What is the purpose of the Catalyst Optimizer and how it works?

items.title: Tungsten (15 min)
items.text: Learn: Spark stores rows as compact binary data and generates Java code for each stage.

items.title: DataFrame vs RDD (15 min)
items.text: Learn: A DataFrame has a schema, so Spark can optimize it; an RDD is a black box to Spark.

links.label: Spark SQL, DataFrames and Datasets Guide

asks: What is the difference between a DataFrame and an RDD?

items.title: Reading a query plan (20 min)
items.text: Learn: The four plans from parsed to physical, and how table statistics change the optimizer's estimates.

title: AQE and how operators run
goal: Explain how each aggregate and sort executes across partitions, and what Spark changes at runtime once it sees real data sizes.

items.title: AQE and the shuffle partitions setting (25 min)
items.text: Learn: AQE re-plans while the query runs, for example by merging small shuffle partitions after a stage ends.
asks: What is an Adaptive Query Execution (AQE)?

items.title: count(distinct) and approx_count_distinct (20 min)
items.text: Learn: An exact distinct count has to shuffle every value; HyperLogLog trades a few percent of error for a tiny sketch.
asks: What is the difference between count() as an action and approx_count_distinct()?

items.title: How avg() and sorting run (25 min)
items.text: Learn: avg keeps a (sum, count) pair per group and merges the pairs; orderBy samples the data, range-partitions it and sorts each part.

links.label: The Internals of Spark SQL: HashAggregateExec
The Internals of Spark SQL: SortExec

title: File formats and data layout
goal: Pick a format, codec and partition layout for a workload, and explain why each choice reads less data.

items.title: Why Parquet and ORC beat CSV (20 min)
items.text: Learn: Columnar files read only the columns you ask for and compress better; CSV is untyped text.
asks: Why is CSV considered a "heavy" format?
What is the difference between Parquet and ORC?

items.title: Predicate pushdown and partitioned folders (20 min)
items.text: Learn: Filters skip row groups using min/max statistics, and partition folders skip whole directories.

items.title: Small files and splittable formats (20 min)
items.text: Learn: Many tiny files waste task time, and a gzip file cannot be split, so one task reads all of it.

items.title: Schema evolution, Avro and Parquet's downsides (20 min)
items.text: Learn: Avro suits streaming and changing schemas; Parquet files cannot be updated in place.
asks: What is the benefit of "Schema Evolution"?
What is the disadvantage of Parquet?

title: Shuffle and joins: how Spark picks a join
goal: Explain what a shuffle costs and how each join algorithm works, predict which one Spark will pick, and change its choice on purpose.
theme: Shuffle and joins: how Spark picks a join
note: This ends week 1. Use the weekend as buffer: finish open items, then re-answer every card you marked on Days 1–5.

items.title: What a shuffle is and what it costs (15 min)
items.text: Learn: A shuffle moves rows between executors through disk and network, and the next stage waits for it.
asks: What is a Shuffle in Spark?
What is the cost of a Shuffle?

items.title: Hash joins: broadcast vs shuffle hash (20 min)
items.text: Learn: Build a hash table from the small side and probe it with the big side; broadcast sends the small table to every executor.

links.label: Performance Tuning: Optimizing the join strategy

asks: When is a Broadcast Join triggered?
What is a "Broadcast Hash Join" vs. a "Shuffle Hash Join"?

items.title: Sort-merge join, Cartesian join and how Spark chooses (25 min)
items.text: Learn: The order in which Spark tries join strategies, and why sort-merge is the default for two big tables.

links.label: The Internals of Spark SQL: JoinSelection

asks: What is a Cartesian Product join?
How does Spark choose which join strategy to use?

items.title: Avoiding shuffles: bucketing and AQE for joins (20 min)
items.text: Learn: Tables bucketed the same way join without a shuffle, and AQE can switch to a broadcast join at runtime.
asks: How can you avoid a shuffle during a Join?
How does AQE help with Joins?

title: Data skew
goal: Spot skew in the Spark UI, explain why it hurts, and choose between AQE, broadcasting, salting, hot-key isolation and repartitioning.

items.title: What data skew is and how to spot it (15 min)
items.text: Learn: One task far slower than the rest means skew: compare the max and the median in the stage's summary metrics.
asks: How do you identify skew in the Spark UI?

items.title: Fixing skew with salting (20 min)
items.text: Learn: Add a random salt to the hot key and replicate the other side, so one big task becomes many small ones.

links.label: How to Fix Data Skew in Apache Spark with the Salting Technique

asks: Name possible ways to solve data skew.
Does filtering data help with skew?

items.title: AQE skew join optimization (10 min)
items.text: Learn: AQE splits a partition that is much bigger than the median, and only for joins.

items.title: repartition, coalesce and read-side skew (15 min)
items.text: Learn: repartition shuffles to even sizes (but a hot key stays together); coalesce only merges partitions without a shuffle.
asks: Can skew happen on the "Read" side?
What is the difference between repartition() and coalesce() regarding skew?
When to use repartition() vs coalesce()?

title: Memory, caching and checkpoints
goal: Draw the executor memory layout from memory, compute each region, and match a symptom (spill, GC time, OOM, killed container) to its fix and to the right persistence tool.

items.title: Executor memory: unified memory, fraction, user memory, off-heap (25 min)
items.text: Learn: Execution and storage share one pool (60% of the heap by default) and borrow from each other; user memory is the rest.
asks: What are the two main memory regions in an Executor?

items.title: Spilling, GC overhead and executor cores (20 min)
items.text: Learn: Too little memory per task means spill to disk or long GC pauses, and more cores per executor means less memory per task.
asks: What is the risk of high spark.executor.cores?

items.title: cache, persist, checkpoint and unpersist (20 min)
items.text: Learn: Cache keeps the lineage and can be recomputed; checkpoint writes the data to storage and cuts the lineage.
asks: What is the difference between checkpoint(), localCheckpoint(), cache() and persist()?
Why limit the use of checkpoint()?

items.title: Fixing a driver out-of-memory error (10 min)
items.text: Learn: Do not collect big results: aggregate first, and know what spark.driver.maxResultSize limits.
asks: How do you fix a "Driver OOM"?

title: Best practices, and late data in streaming
goal: Name the habits that make a Spark job fast and easy to maintain, with the reason for each, and explain how a stream handles late events.
theme: Best practices, and late data in streaming

items.title: Why avoid UDFs, use built-in functions (20 min)
items.text: Learn: A Python UDF is a black box that blocks optimizations and sends every row to a Python process.

links.label: PySpark guide: Unleashing UDFs and UDTFs

asks: Why should you use standard Spark SQL functions over Python logic?

items.title: Broadcast variables and the star schema (15 min)
items.text: Learn: Send small lookup data once per executor, and join one big fact table to small dimension tables by broadcast.
asks: What is the "Star Schema" benefit in Spark?

items.title: Loops with lit(), hardcoded values and data lineage (15 min)
items.text: Learn: Each withColumn adds a projection, so loops build huge plans; use one select and keep settings in config files.
asks: How do you handle "Data Lineage" in Spark?
What is the best way to handle "Hardcoded" values?

items.title: Late data in streaming (20 min)
items.text: Learn: A watermark says how late data may be, so Spark can finish windows and drop old state.

links.label: Structured Streaming: Handling late data and watermarking

asks: How to handle "Late Data" in streaming?

title: Delta Lake
goal: Explain how Delta Lake turns a folder of Parquet files into a transactional table, and what each DML and maintenance command writes to the data folder and to the log.

items.title: The transaction log, ACID and snapshot isolation (25 min)
items.text: Learn: Every commit is a JSON file in _delta_log, so readers always see one consistent version of the table.

links.label: Diving Into Delta Lake: Unpacking the Transaction Log

items.title: Schema enforcement, UPDATE, DELETE and MERGE (20 min)
items.text: Learn: Delta rewrites only the files that contain changed rows, and MERGE does an upsert in one atomic step.

links.label: Delta Lake: Table deletes, updates, and merges

asks: Can you run SQL UPDATE and DELETE on Delta?

items.title: OPTIMIZE, Z-ordering and VACUUM (20 min)
items.text: Learn: OPTIMIZE compacts small files, Z-order groups similar values together, and VACUUM deletes files no table version needs.

items.title: Change Data Feed (10 min)
items.text: Learn: CDF records which rows were inserted, updated or deleted in each version, so you can load only the changes.

items.title: Set up Zillacode on your Mac (once, about 20 min)
items.text: zillacode.com no longer runs problems: Zillacode is open source now and runs locally with Docker. Start Docker Desktop, then in a terminal: `git clone https://github.com/davidzajac1/zillacode.git`, `cd zillacode`, `docker compose up`. The first start downloads about 2.6 GB. Open the problem list, open problem 1, choose PySpark and press Run on the starter code to check that it works. Ports 5001, 5173 and 8081–8083 must be free; stop it with Ctrl+C. Then solve the 52 problems at your own pace, Easy first; the last cell of today's notebook lists them by topic.
